All teams ↗

Make a metric answer inspectable

The same metric name can mean different populations, periods, and calculations. Maia can answer from an approved report or supplied output and include the definition, filters, source, and refresh time beside the value.

That context lets the requester use the answer responsibly. If the report does not contain the requested cohort or the definition is unclear, Maia should ask a question rather than produce a plausible number.

Scope the request before analysis begins

Many Slack questions arrive as "Can you pull the numbers?" Maia can use the team's intake rubric to ask what decision the analysis supports, which population matters, what period to use, and at what grain the answer should be delivered.

The result is a short analysis brief with the business question, decision owner, defined measures, available datasets, assumptions, and desired output. The analyst accepts or reframes it before investing time in a query or model.

Explain approved outputs

Supply a final chart, table, or report with its definitions and filters. Maia can draft a stakeholder narrative that names the main changes, caveats, and follow-up questions. It should distinguish an observed association from a causal explanation and keep unsupported reasons out.

The analyst validates the statistical and business interpretation. Maia helps carry that interpretation into the Slack discussion without replacing the governed model or the analyst's review.

Distribute recurring digests

For a weekly metric digest, define the approved report, recipients, comparison period, and alert thresholds. Maia can post only values that changed materially or crossed a threshold, along with the source timestamp.

This gives teams a concise entry point into the report. The data owner chooses the thresholds and audience. Row-level or report permissions still matter when deciding what can appear in a channel.

Route data quality questions

Validation outputs can produce a long list of failures with little business context. Give Maia the checks, dataset definitions, ownership map, and recent changes. It can group related exceptions, identify affected reports, and prepare questions for the responsible owner.

The analyst confirms the affected scope and chooses remediation. This workflow stops at the quality packet; the data team makes and verifies any warehouse change.

Start with one governed report

Choose a report whose definitions and refresh behavior are known. Include a missing cohort or stale refresh. Ask Maia the same question an operator would ask in Slack, then verify that the limitation appears prominently beside the answer.

The Slack answer can also show the report owner and the best route for a follow-up. Requesters know whether to ask about the business definition, refresh schedule, or source data, and analysts receive a better framed question when deeper work is needed.

Questions from data teams

Can Maia query our warehouse?

That depends on the connected tool or custom access configured for your workspace. A supplied report output is enough to begin with a governed answer.

Does Maia create metrics?

Maia can help draft a definition for discussion, but the data team approves and implements metrics in the governed system.

What happens when a metric is undefined?

Maia should state the ambiguity and ask for the owner or definition. It should not substitute a familiar formula without approval.
